conventions.convention: Smooth programs have n ≥ 1, an open domain, C² objective and componentwise C² constraints. Inequalities are g_i ≤ 0; gradients are columns; L = f + νᵀh + λᵀg with λ ≥ 0. Zero equality and inequality counts use empty maps and vacuous conditions.

The critical cone at a KKT tuple is the linearized cone intersected with directions satisfying ∇f(x)ᵀd = 0. MFCQ includes full row rank of Dh and a kernel direction strictly decreasing every active inequality.
The convex dual infimizes the Lagrangian over the common function domain D, including when some inequality multiplier is zero. Only domain-preserving removable inequalities are deleted.

Slater requires an equality-feasible point in the intersection of the individual relative-interior domains, strictly satisfying every remaining inequality. Equality rows are independent; the strong-duality theorem separately assumes a finite attained primal value.

The outward normal cone consists of v with ⟨v,y−x⟩ ≤ 0 for every y in C. The KKT residual is the sum of five Euclidean norms, including inequality violation, negative multiplier violation, and componentwise complementarity; empty-vector norms are zero.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the C² inequality program, feasible and active sets, Bouligand and linearized cones, LICQ, MFCQ, Lagrangian, KKT system, and critical cone with g_i ≤ 0 and λ_i ≥ 0.
On an open convex domain, for differentiable convex objective and inequalities and affine equalities, a feasible KKT tuple with λ ≥ 0 gives a global minimizer x_* and −∇f(x_*) ∈ N_C(x_*).
For A ∈ R^(r×n) and b ∈ R^r, exactly one holds: Ax = b for some x ≥ 0; or Aᵀy ≥ 0 and bᵀy < 0 for some y.
Every primal feasible x and dual feasible (λ,ν) satisfy q(λ,ν) ≤ f_0(x). Consequently, when the primal feasible set is nonempty, d* ≤ p*.
For the defined C² program, MFCQ at a feasible x implies T_C(x) = L_C(x).
A convex p:V → (−∞,+∞] on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, never −∞ and finite somewhere, with 0 ∈ ri(dom p) and p(0) real, admits a linear functional ℓ with p(z) ≥ p(0) + ℓ(z) for every z ∈ V.
For C² H with DH(x) surjective, d ∈ ker DH(x) and DH(x)z + D²H(x)[d,d] = 0 are realized by a C² curve on H = H(x) with value x, velocity d, and acceleration z. The q = 0 case is included.

For the defined C² program, a feasible KKT tuple whose Lagrangian Hessian is strictly positive on every nonzero critical direction gives a strict local minimizer. No constraint qualification is assumed, and the condition is vacuous for critical cone {0}.

alerts.finding: alg-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-multiplier-method contains a separate '## Proof' proving a termination property. Step 2.1 states: 'the cap $K$ forces a return after at most $KM$ inner iterations and $K$ outer tests.' The dispatch's Algorithms rule requires termination and other properties in separate proved result items. The finite-cap argument itself is sound, but its placement in this algorithm item conflicts with that structural rule.

seams_checked.note: The contact definition and normal-cone resolvent lemma preserve the outward normal inequality. The contact definition explicitly supplies the empty operator value outside C, where the supplier only defines normals on C.

The optimality proof uses g = −x, ν = −y and nonnegative reduced-cost multipliers, verifying every convex KKT hypothesis. Phase I preserves the exact Farkas signs Aᵀq ≥ 0 and bᵀq < 0. Zero-dimensional optimality is handled separately.

The fixed-point theorem uses the outward normal convention and invokes convex KKT sufficiency only in the multiplier-to-optimum direction. It separately treats n = 0 and asserts no multiplier converse.

The listed page has no direct citation of an owned item and makes no KKT or multiplier assertion. Its projection and convex-function interfaces introduce no conflicting sign convention or strengthened use of this page.

Smooth inequalities and multipliers preserve the supplier signs. The QP certificate explicitly translates to g(w) = −w, λ = s and ν = −y before weak duality. The central-path theorem defines its open-domain dual q_D explicitly and proves the needed weak bound there.
The consensus ADMM example applies the dual definition and weak duality to finite convex quadratics with the independent equality row (1,−1). Its saddle and dual optimum are also computed directly.

The relaxation interface requires the supplier's convex-program representation. The box-bound theorem uses only weak duality at an embedded feasible point and a verified lower bound ℓ ≤ q; it assumes neither strong duality nor solver success.

Definitions preserve g ≤ 0, λ ≥ 0, the Lagrangian, and residual components. The convex QP lemma uses Farkas directly for polyhedral multiplier existence and convex KKT only for sufficiency, without adding an MFCQ requirement. Local methods retain their own LICQ, complementarity and curvature hypotheses.

Transcription residuals preserve stationarity, inequality and multiplier violation, and complementarity signs. The local SQP theorem quotes strict positivity on nonzero critical directions faithfully and separately assumes actual C³ NLP functions, LICQ, strict complementarity and a sufficiently close start.

No direct owned-item citation occurs on the A page. Its finite SQP branch inherits the active KKT convention through the SQP supplier and distinguishes a linear-system residual certificate from nonlinear KKT, feasibility and optimality claims.
